title: Error layer: problem+json, error registry, error handler
goal: Every HTTP error leaves the API as RFC 9457 problem+json with a stable registry code, request_id and correct retry hints, thrown through typed errors instead of strings.
scope_in: Error registry module built from the errors.json output of B003: `ErrorCode` union, `status`, default `title` and `retryable` per code.

`AppError` class (code, detail, errors[], retryAfterS, cause) plus helpers: `badRequest`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `notFound`, `conflict`, `unprocessable`, `tooManyRequests`, `unavailable`, `validationFailed(errors)`.

Fastify error handler plugin (apps/api/src/plugins/error-handler.ts) and not-found handler producing `application/problem+json` with `type` `https://centcom.dev/errors/<code>`, `instance` (route path), `request_id`, and `retry_after_s` + `Retry-After` for 429/503/retryable codes.
Mapping of validation failures from B003 validators to `errors[]` with JSON Pointer; mapping of unknown thrown errors to a generic 500 without leaking message or stack.
`toProblem(err, ctx)` pure function shared with the relay for `sys.error` frame bodies (same shape per CT-ERR).
scope_out: The WebSocket `sys.error` frame sending logic (relay lanes).
Rate-limit and idempotency decisions (B023, B024) which only throw errors from this layer.
build_against: Fastify `inject()` with throwaway routes that throw each error type; registry loaded from the generated JSON in packages/contracts.
interfaces: `class AppError extends Error { code: ErrorCode; status: number; detail?: string; errors?: FieldError[]; retryAfterS?: number }`.
`interface Problem { type: string; title: string; status: number; code: string; detail?: string; instance?: string; request_id: string; retry_after_s?: number; errors?: FieldError[] }`.
`toProblem(err: unknown, ctx: {requestId: string; instance?: string}): Problem`.
`isRetryable(status: number, method: string, hasIdempotencyKey: boolean): boolean` implementing the CT-ERR retry table.
acceptance: A thrown `forbidden()` yields HTTP 403, `content-type: application/problem+json`, body with `code:'forbidden'`, `status:403`, `request_id` equal to the `X-Request-Id` header.
A schema validation failure yields a body whose `errors[0].pointer` is a JSON Pointer such as `/events/3/qty`.
429 and 503 problems carry `retry_after_s` (integer) and a matching `Retry-After` header; 400/403/404 never do.
An unexpected `TypeError` yields 500 with a generic detail; the original message appears only in the server log (redacted), and the response contains no stack or file path.
Unknown route yields 404 problem; wrong method yields 405 problem with `Allow` header; body larger than 256 KiB yields 413-class problem; malformed JSON yields 400 problem.
`detail` strings never contain the request body or header values (test with a body containing a bearer token).
`isRetryable(503,'POST',false)` is false and `isRetryable(503,'GET',false)` is true; 429 on POST without a key is not retryable.
tests: problem.test.ts: shape for every registry code (table-driven).
leak.test.ts: secrets in request never appear in response or log output.
guardrails: MUST only emit `code` values present in the registry generated from contracts; MUST NOT invent codes.
MUST NOT include stack traces, SQL, file paths, other users' data or secrets in `detail`.
MUST set `request_id` on every problem, including errors raised before routing.
MUST give uniform timing/shape for auth failures (same body structure whether the user exists or not).
failure_modes: Error occurs while serialising an error -> fall back to a static minimal 500 problem body.
Code missing from registry -> handler logs an error and responds with the status-class generic code (CT-ERR rule 7).
Reply already sent (stream) -> log and destroy the socket, do not write a second response.
